profile.reading:
This is Equinix's WA3 facility at Aleje Jerozolimskie 213 in the Salomea district of Warsaw, Poland; this row carried no operator website URL on file until a same-day research pass located Equinix's dedicated WA3 page by matching the URL pattern already on file for sibling Italy and Finland rows, substituting Poland's country and region path segments. That page describes WA3 as a three-story, reinforced-concrete building with 1,400 square meters, about 15,069 square feet, of colocation space, N+1 power and cooling redundancy, generator autonomy of 30 hours or more at full load, and a 99.9999%-plus global uptime guarantee, though it does not publish a specific IT capacity figure in megawatts or kilowatts. Equinix entered the European colocation market through its 2007 acquisition of IXEurope and expanded further through its 2015 acquisition of TelecityGroup for about $3.8 billion, though Equinix's current WA3 page does not attribute the building to either predecessor company by name. Equinix, founded in Silicon Valley in 1998, converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX; the company's own about page states a current global footprint of 281 data centers across six continents, while Wikipedia separately cites approximately 260 data centers across 33 countries as of 2025.

As an EU-based facility, this data center falls under the European Union's Energy Efficiency Directive reporting requirements, which since 2024 have required data centers above a minimum capacity threshold to report power usage effectiveness, water usage, and other sustainability metrics to a European Commission database, part of a broader EU push for standardized data center energy transparency that does not have a direct equivalent in most of the US markets covered elsewhere in this registry.
